messages:
priya: Starting a PRD intake for a feature I'm calling 'latency slabs' — goal is per-route latency budgets + cost-aware aborts. Problem statement: customers want predictable tail latency under bursty traffic without doubling token costs. I sketched goals / non-goals / acceptance criteria below, looking for feedback.

 dan: Short summary — which customers pushed this?

 priya: Two pilots: ShopLoop (search-heavy, high QPS) and AcmeDocs (chat with long contexts). They asked for: search route P99 <= 200ms, chat P95 <= 500ms, and any cost uplift must be <= ~15% or clearly explainable tradeoff.

 alex: To be explicit: runtime would enforce a per-route "slab" (soft budget) via adaptive batching + preemptive aborts, with optional fallback to a cheaper model. Is that what we're proposing?

 priya: Yes. Rough proposal: 1) a per-route latency_slab config (budget + priority), 2) runtime control that attempts to meet budget via batching, prefix caching, and preemptive aborts, 3) structured error on abort: `{"code": "latency_budget_exceeded", "recovery": "retry_or_stale_cache"}`. Also telemetry labels for reason.

 sarah: Acceptance criteria (initial thoughts):
- For pilot routes, measured P99 (24h) <= configured target.
- Under a synthetic spike (5x normal qps for 5 minutes) the error/failure rate stays <= 1.5x baseline for that route.
- Cost delta (tokens + infra) for pilot routes <= +15% vs baseline OR product shows clear cost/quality tradeoff doc and opt-in.

 maria: Non-goals (callouts): not a fix for model quality regressions, not replacing autoscaling/cluster provisioning (we rely on existing Dedicated/Hosted autoscale), not cross-tenant QoS guarantees. Also not supporting complex multi-turn streaming rollback in v1.

 dan: Edge cases we should enumerate: long-running streaming responses, function-calls that happen mid-stream, KV-cache cold misses, tenants that pin very large seq-lens. Need defined behavior for each.

 alex: My takes on streaming: prefer to let in-flight tokens finish, but emit a `budget-warning` event (header) when slab is close, and if abort is necessary, finish kernel-level tokens then send a structured partial-response marker so SDKs can detect truncation. We should add SDK guidance.

 infra-bot: deploy-bot: FYI — config-service will get a new feature flag `latency_slab` and a per-route config proto. Please include config-schema PR in infra repo.

 priya: Questions for product review: 1) GA success metric: propose 2 paying pilots running >=3 weeks meeting SLOs. 2) Rollout plan: pilot -> staged beta (5 customers) -> GA after safety review and runbook sign-off. 3) Telemetry: per-request labels + sampling of full traces for failed/aborted requests.

 sarah: :thumbsup: I can own the runbook + eval harness (synthetic spike tests). I'll draft test cases (cold cache, sustained spike, bursty tail) and link to eval repo.

 maria: I'll draft non-goals and security considerations (KMS labels, audit logs for aborted responses). Also recommend an opt-in toggle per-tenant + explicit telemetry tags.

 priya: Next steps: Sarah + Maria + Alex to produce a one-pager PRD outline by EOW with config proto sketch and acceptance checklist. Dan to coordinate pilot contacts. I will schedule a 30m sync after the draft. :eyes:

 dan: I'll loop in pilot contacts (will ping @john.shoploop and @linda.acme next week).

 alex: I'll add SDK guidance notes and a short example snippet for partial-response handling:
```
// SDK behavior on partial responses
if (resp.error?.code === 'latency_budget_exceeded') {
  // surface to app: consider stale cache or retry with lower seq-len
}
```

 priya: Thanks all — if no objections I'll mark this as PRD intake draft and set owners. :+1:

 maria: No objections from me.

 sarah: OK from me.

 priya: Marking owners: sarah (runbook & harness), alex (SDK + partial response format), maria (security + non-goals), dan (pilot coordination). PRD draft due EOW.
